question: GQ-004
subject: the tenth deferral — "a copyright determination, not mine to make"
the_deferral: "A 1900 Twain edition is almost certainly public domain despite absent metadata — and asserting that is a copyright determination, not a query fix. It is not mine to make on someone else's behalf, however confident I am."
verdict_on_the_deferral: STANDS. Asserting a work is public domain when its metadata does not say so is a legal judgement, and confidence is not authority.

what_it_obscured.question_i_never_asked: How many candidates need NO determination because IA has already made it?
what_it_obscured.query: mediatype:texts AND rights:"public domain" AND language:eng NOT collection:printdisabled NOT collection:inlibrary
what_it_obscured.reading: Every one of those 270,049 carries an EXPLICIT rights field set by the Internet Archive. Ingesting them requires no determination by me — the determination is already recorded upstream. The pool grew by 3 since 06:43 today, so it is live.

the_correction: The deferral is true and was doing extra work. It reads as "IA expansion is blocked on a copyright call", when what is blocked is only the SPARSE-METADATA subset — the Twain case. A quarter of a million texts with explicit rights are not blocked on anything I cannot decide.
what_is_actually_blocked: Selection, not rights. I measured this earlier: the head of the explicit pool is ephemera — student newspapers, sales catalogues, family photographs. The open question is which of 270,049 the Library wants, and that is a curation decision, not a legal one.
